successors.name: Spanish Empire
successors.text: 'In 1543 it officially became the governorship of Michoacán'

ledger.x: c. 1300: Tariacuri founds the Tarascan state round Lake Patzcuaro. 'installed his sons Hiripan and Tangaxuan as lords of Ihuatzio and Tzintzuntzan respectively'; Tariacuri ruled from Patzcuaro; 'The kingdom was founded in the early 14th century'. The Michoacan page: he united the…
c. 1350: the whole Patzcuaro basin is one state. 'By the death of Tariacuri (around 1350), his lineage was in control of all the major centers around Lake Patzcuaro.'
Tarascan conquests grow the kingdom threefold.
1455: the Tarascans invade the Toluca Valley.
1460: the Tarascans reach the Pacific at Zacatula.
1472: the Aztecs recover the Toluca Valley.
1475: Aztec raiders take frontier towns of eastern Michoacan.
1480: the Tarascans begin to occupy Colima and Jalisco.
1522: a Spanish force under Cristobal de Olid enters Purepecha territory.
14 February 1530: Nuño de Guzman kills Tangaxoan II and the Tarascan kingdom passes to New Spain.
14 February 1530: end of the Tarascan state, 'the last king of a sovereign kingdom, Tangaxuan II'.

wars.name: Tarascan conquests of the neighbours
wars.outcome: 'Conquest of neighboring tribes and territories occurred between 1401 and 1450'; Zacatula on the Pacific in 1460; Colima and Jalisco partly occupied in 1480-1510.

wars.name: Aztec-Tarascan wars
wars.outcome: The Tarascans invaded the Toluca Valley in 1455 and lost it in 1472; they defeated Axayacatl in 1476 and 1479 and an Aztec invasion in 1515 'failed to take any territory'.

wars.name: Spanish conquest of Michoacán
wars.outcome: A Spanish force under Cristobal de Olid entered in 1522; Nuño de Guzman killed Tangaxoan II in 1530 ('the king was executed on February 14, 1530'); the land became the governorship of Michoacán in 1543.

certainty.note: A tributary kingdom with fortified frontier posts; no border is dated or surveyed.
